_note: Failure gallery. 'viz' names the chart the page draws from data/rl.json, data/llm.json or data/terrariabench.json; 'replay' links a step in an audited LLM tape; 'video' and 'videos' name official-Terraria recordings from data/videos.json with a start time in game seconds. Numbers in 'facts' are copied from the cited reports.

items.title: LLMs spend a third of their actions on moves that cannot happen
items.text: Every primitive action costs a game tick, legal or not. Luna's attempts include mining empty cells, jumping under a ceiling, walking into walls and climbing rope that is not there. Interrupting the batch after the first illegal action cut the illegal fraction from 46.2% (compact16) to 11.8%, at about three times the calls per action.

items.title: A rope that is not there: 239 climbing attempts in one episode
items.text: On world 31,000,011 Luna issued 170 illegal 'climb up' and 69 illegal 'climb down' actions. The batch interface hides intermediate feedback, so one wrong belief about the rope repeats for up to 16 actions per call.

replay.note: Episode ends in death at step 1,802.

items.title: LLMs build a workshop, then die
items.text: Both long Luna episodes reached a furnace and smelted copper, then died (scores 20 and 19). Five of eight harness-study attempts died before 2,000 actions; the three survivors were stopped by the dollar guard, so none completed 3,000 actions. The final PPO configurations die in 1% to 9% of episodes.

replay.note: Furnace at step 2,020, copper bar at 2,035, death at 2,478.

items.title: PPO goes deep and never comes back, on some seeds
items.text: Return to surface needs the agent to climb back up after mining deep. The same configuration learns it on one training seed and not at all on another: the bars show worlds (of 128) where each seed's final policy returned to the surface.

items.title: Iron bars spent on a second anvil
items.text: An anvil costs iron bars that the pickaxe and chainmail also need. Every seed of the generic gamma .9998 arm crafts 1.7 to 1.9 anvils per episode on average and holds up to four at once; across all v8 runs the peak is five or six. Each extra anvil burns bars that would have gone into the next tool.
items.source: data/rl.json (diag.json: anvil crafts per episode, anvil inventory peak)

items.title: The iron pickaxe is a stockpiling problem
items.text: Diagnostics count episodes where crafting the iron pickaxe was legal at least once. In almost every run that number is 0 to 3 of 128: the policy never holds enough iron bars at once (median peak 5 to 8). The 4B and 6B shaped runs that do stockpile craft it in every single world where it becomes legal.

items.title: Carrying a workbench for 38,031 actions and placing it on 958
items.text: On v4 a recurrent policy carried a bench for 38,031 actions with a valid placement spot on every one, but selected it on only 958, so the furnace recipe (4 wood, 20 stone, 3 torches and a bench in range) was never satisfied in 128 worlds. The successful MLP crafted on all 181 legal opportunities.

items.title: Twice the world, six points lower
items.text: Doubling the world width to 256 tiles with the standard arm dropped the 2B score from 25.45 to 19.45. Longer episodes and better arms recover most of it, but not all: wider worlds are a navigation problem PPO does not solve with an 11x9 view.

items.title: Up to half the episode spent after the last unlock
items.text: After the last achievement, the final policies keep acting for about 300 to 1,650 steps on average (of 3,000) without unlocking anything: the remaining achievements are out of their reach, and the reward gives no gradient toward them. The generic gamma .9998 arm has the shortest idle tail.

items.title: Official Terraria: "The workbench is placed", and it is not
items.text: The observer mod journals every crafted and placed object, so the score never depends on what the model says. Haiku crafts a work bench within the first minute of almost every run and then reports it as placed, sometimes with the achievement it would have earned. The journal shows the craft and no placement. The quotes are the models' own messages at the game time shown.

video.note: Haiku paused on world 402: the bench is crafted at 0:24 and the message at 0:25 calls it placed.

items.source: TerrariaBench/experiments/landscape-2026-11-08.md; evidence/timeline.md and observer journal of each run

items.title: Official Terraria: in real time, slow models die again and again
items.text: With normal enemies and the clock running, every second of model latency is a second the character stands still. Luna and Terra take about 6 to 7 s per call, so they see the game once every 6 to 7 game seconds; after nightfall zombies and demon eyes kill them faster than they react. Luna died 17 times in 20 minutes on world 403. Pausing the game during model calls helps some models (Opus on world 401: 4 deaths paused against 17 in real time) but not all: paused Luna still died 11 and 14 times, because night still comes.

video.note: Luna in real time on world 403; the buttons jump to each death.

items.source: TerrariaBench/experiments/landscape-2026-11-08.md (b05, b04, b06r, c1, c2); observer journal death events

items.title: Official Terraria: Terra leaves the world through Save & Exit
items.text: Nothing in the prompt mentions the game menu, and Terra opened it anyway and chose Save & Exit: at 16:04 in real time (default-v1, where re-entering the world crashed tModLoader) and at 1:41 in a paused run (default-v2, where it re-entered three times while the harness kept calling the model with the game clock stopped, $0.96 lost). default-v2 now ends a run when the journal reports that the player left the world; the remaining time is forfeited, not censored.

videos.note: default-v1, real time, world 402: the menu opens at about 16:00.
default-v2, paused, world 403: Save & Exit at 1:41; the video ends with the world.

items.title: Official Terraria: Haiku stops playing and writes summaries
items.text: Paused Haiku reads the game time in every tool result, knows the session length and starts writing end-of-session summaries instead of calling the tool. With thinking on, the API cannot force a tool call. On world 403 it declared at 12:35 that it would take no further actions and repeated a final-state summary until the end: 338 of its 571 replies had no action, and each was executed as a 1-second wait, so the last 7.5 minutes passed as about 300 waits. The no-action rule keeps such runs bounded and scored; it cannot make the model act.

video.note: From 12:20: the character stands still while the waits run out the clock.

items.title: Official Terraria: runs that do not count, and why
items.text: As on terrariabench.com, runs stay listed with their reason instead of disappearing. A run is not scored when the harness or the provider failed; it is censored when a dollar cap stopped it before 20 game-minutes, and then keeps what it reached. No default-v2 run has shown direct tile control; the observer is read-only and input goes through the X server like a keyboard and mouse.
